payload.headline: Micron falls 2.1% to 690.44, now below its 703.86 zero-growth value

summary.thesis: The business is at a record level of profit and holds 40.6B of net cash, but the price is falling because the market doubts that the peak 74.59% operating margin will last.
summary.decision: Long term: hold, and add only if the price reaches the support zone near 658.32. Swing: wait, because the trend is down and the 2026-12-23 report is close.
summary.act_at: Add at 658.32, trim above 833.11, switch to wait on a close below 643.69

payload.happening: MU closed at 690.44, down 2.1% on the day. The trend is down: the price is under its falling 20-day average of 800.8 and its 50-day average of 919.8. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2026-12-23.
payload.business: Nothing today changes the business. The latest quarter, which ended 2026-09-03, showed revenue up 345.03% from a year earlier and up 30.81% from the quarter before. The gross margin was 80.72%, and free cash flow over the past year was 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The balance sheet is strong, with 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt. This price drop is about sentiment: the broader tech market is in a downtrend and fear is elevated. What is at risk is how long the margin lasts. Operating margin rose to 74.59% from 26.14%, and the filings note that it sits at the top of its 5-year range of -41% to 75%. Memory chips go through boom-and-bust price cycles (general knowledge), so profits this high can fade fast. The company's survival is not at risk. With 40.6B of net cash, it can get through a downturn. A governance note: insiders sold $14.0M outside their pre-set trading plans. That is often for personal reasons and says nothing direct about demand.

worth.text: The data gives no DCF (discounted cash flow, a valuation based on future cash) because free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a one-year jump like that can't be projected forward. The test that does work asks what the price assumes. At this price, the market expects free cash flow to start shrinking slightly, with implied starting growth of -0.5%. If cash flow simply holds flat, the value is 703.86, slightly above today's price. The two methods disagree because of one question: is 59.0B of cash flow normal, or a peak? Judged on its own price-to-sales history, the stock looks expensive. Judged against similar companies, it looks cheap: price-to-sales is 5.9 versus a peer median of 8.0, and the trailing price-to-earnings ratio is 9.3. Even if operating margin falls to 37%, the value is 779.6, but that figure assumes 20% starting growth. My fair-value range is 703.86 to 833.11.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near today's 59.0B instead of shrinking sharply as the 74.59% operating margin fades from its 5-year peak.

bull: At 690.44, the price sits below the 703.86 value that assumes zero growth, so the market already expects cash flow to shrink slightly (-0.5% implied starting growth).
Price-to-sales of 5.9 is below the peer median of 8.0, and the trailing price-to-earnings ratio is only 9.3.
Net cash of 40.6B and a 44.27% free-cash-flow margin give a large cushion if memory prices weaken.
bear: Operating margin of 74.59% is at the top of its 5-year range of -41% to 75%, up from 26.14%. Peaks like this usually fade.
The price is in a downtrend, below a falling 50-day average of 919.8, and the put-to-call open interest ratio of 2.03 shows traders buying downside protection.

levels.what: Top of the 643.69–658.32 support zone, which has held twice. At this price the stock is well below the 703.86 zero-growth value. This is the level to add.
Top of the own-history valuation range. Above it, the price depends on peak margins lasting. This is the level to trim.
Bottom of the support zone. A close below it would signal the market doubts the margins and would move the call from hold to wait.

longterm.why: At 690.44 the price is just under the 703.86 zero-growth value, and the business has not changed. The downtrend argues for adding at 658.32 rather than now.

swing.why: The trend is down, and resistance at 730.45–745.08 is less than one 58.5 ATR (average daily price range) above the price, so the upside is too small for the risk. Enter only if the 643.69–658.32 support holds on a test, or on a close above 745.08.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-23 report comes after the 2026-12-18 options expiry, which prices a 17.1% move, and before the 2027-02-19 expiry, which prices 27.1%. A new position taken before the report carries that event risk, and the report's operating margin will set the next leg of the price.

change_mind: A close below 643.69 would break the support zone. That would move the long-term call from hold to wait, with the next support at 463.68–478.31.
A close above 745.08 would clear the first resistance zone and turn the swing call to enter, with a target at 803.87.

If the 2026-12-23 report shows operating margin falling from 74.59% toward 37%, the value depends on 20% growth holding (779.6). Without that growth, the 490.66 own-history mid becomes the anchor and hold turns to wait.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold. The 2.1% drop to 690.44 took the price below the 703.86 zero-growth value but not yet down to the 658.32 add level, and there was no news that changes the business.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
